title: Roter Sand

nativeAxes.origin: Native+X east,+Z south; heading0 preserves the GMG survey south180/WNW292.5/NE45-degree bays, ENE67.5/WSW247.5-degree ladders and SSE157.5/NNW337.5-degree caisson long axis.

visualBrief: Offshore riveted taper with black plinth, white/red/white shaft, red service room and three unequal-height round bays; white lantern, black domes, scalloped gallery, portholes, rivets, ladders, davit and mooring dolphins.

sourceFacts.survey: GMG GA218014, 14 June 2019, section 1.02 pp I-5–7; field visits October 2018 and May 2019
sourceFacts.verticalDatum: GMG III-9 uses low water = NN -2.05 m; tower tip NN +28.90 m
sourceFacts.basis: 2018–2019 surveyed offshore exterior. Above-water caisson is reconstructed from two7.3m-radius arcs with3.6m circle-center separation, approximately11x14m; bay offset is reconstructed from published1.9m diameter/270-degree exposed arcs and5.1m central service-room diameter. These rounded facts are not a fabrication survey. Exact corrosion/fasteners, submerged caisson, hidden interior and operating optics excluded. Static viewer water zero approximates historical NN; local floor datum−2.05m is explicit and no tide/datum conversion is claimed. limitations: Medium-fi exterior of the 2018–2019 surveyed offshore appearance. The original detailed master remains separately reproducible; review-scope.json selects the refined exterior and four browser derivatives.

Caisson arcs, exposed bay joins and principal dimensions follow the rounded engineering facts. Seam/rivet spacing, porthole allocation, small fittings and battery cupboard remain reconstructions, not a fabrication survey.

Street/close-up/master levels have real recessed circular apertures. District/skyline windows become marks; far rail and curve subdivisions reduce while retaining the complete tower. Hidden interiors, underwater foundations, exact corrosion and working lamp optics are omitted.

Exact offshore identity and compass directions are survey-backed. Viewer water zero approximates historical NN; elevation -2.05 m is explicit, with no tidal or geodetic conversion. The owner’s 2026 plan describes a future relocation, not a documented completed move.
